THE SHAPES (neutral reproducers, run on the tree, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    my $text = "b1 a2 c3";
    my @s = sort $text =~ /\w\d/g;
    print "@s\n";
    perl: a2 b1 c3
    PCL : PCL: statement dropped at ... line 2: ... -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case: []

    for (3) { print join(",", sort $_ > 0 ? 1..$_ : $_..1), "\n" }
    perl: 1,2,3
    PCL : PCL: statement dropped ... -- Handle single node of unknown type.

    my $n = 3;
    my @s = sort $n > 0 ? (3, 1, 2) : (9);
    print "@s\n";
    perl: 1 2 3
    PCL : Unhandled undefined-function ... The function COMMON-LISP:NIL is undefined.  + a Lisp backtrace (exit 1)
          (`sort $n + 1, 0` the same; perl: 0 3)

    Controls that work: `sort($text =~ /\w\d/g)` and `sort($n > 0 ? ... : ...)` (parenthesised).

WHERE (emitted Lisp, the third shape): `(p-sort (let ...) (p-if ...))` -- the `$n` became the comparator form (a `let` that
evaluates to nil) and the expression's remainder the list, so p-sort FUNCALLs nil.  perl's rule (toke.c, after `sort`): a
`$var` is the SUBREF only when the next token starts a term of the list; an infix operator after it makes it the first
operand of the LIST expression.  With `$_` (a Magic token) the parse falls through to a drop instead.
UNTIDY half: the raw `undefined-function` condition is an internal error that reaches the user (#1427's census).

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (taken): 0841 with its two sorts parenthesised (`sort($names =~ ...)`) and 1308 with
`sort($_ > 0 ? ... : ...)` are byte-identical to perl -- the only cause of both.

PROGRAMS: 0841-Merge-and-aggregate-datasets, 1308-Sort-numbers-lexicographically.


=== DONE (s543x) ===
perl's `sort SUBREF LIST` is `LSTOP indirob listexpr`; the lexer reads the slot after the scalar with toke.c's ONE
indirect-object rule (case '$', print's filehandle slot too): the scalar is the comparator exactly when a TERM follows.
FIX (Pl/PExpr.pm): ONE predicate `_sort_scalar_is_comparator` (= print's `_is_scalar_fh_token` + `_is_print_term_start`)
and ONE node builder `_sort_scalar_comparator`, asked by the bare form and by the parenthesised one (`sort($by @l)` was a
drop: the paren arm had no scalar case).  `_is_print_term_start` gains the sign rule (`+`/`-` glued after whitespace
starts a term) -- it also closes #405's residue.  PPI half: PCL's branch group BN (Â§80, `f687c2ae` + `a8178635`): sort
joins `%FILEHANDLE_LISTOP` (`-1` `.5` `%h` `*FH` `/re/` lex as terms in the slot) and a `<` glued to a name after the
slot's scalar is a readline (print's slot too).  Runtime: `p-sort-get-fn` dies "Not a subroutine reference" /
"Undefined sort subroutine \"PKG::NAME\" called" where the comparator FUNCALLed NIL (raw).
DECISION TABLE (what follows the scalar -> perl / base / tree): @l, 3, (3,1,2), $x(..), %h, &f, f1(), "s", qw(), $n,
<FH>, /re/, -1, +1, .5, \@l, !1, ~1, a word -> SUBREF / SUBREF except %h .5 (drops) and the paren form (drop) /
SUBREF; `,` `=~` `>` `?` `+ ` `- ` `.` `x` `..` `*` `/ ` `%` `==` `<` `eq` `cmp` `||` `//` `and` `or` `=>` `->` `[..]`
`{..}` `;` / end of list -> LIST / SUBREF (drops, raw NIL, or the first element silently lost: `sort $p, $q` = ($q))
/ LIST.  Probes scratch/s543x/probes/m1-*.pl: m1-probe 54/58, m1-paren 33/34, m1-print 24/28 (the rest: stderr
order of a deliberate die), m1-rl 4/4, m1-rt 12/20 (perl = tree on the tree-only rows).  Rosetta 0841 1308 `same`.
LEFT (filed / known): #5620 a CODE ref heading `sort LIST` is taken as the comparator by p-sort's run-time guess (rare);
#5622 `sort $$r LIST` (a scalar deref in the slot) is a drop (rare); a bad comparator with a list of fewer than two
elements is not checked (perl checks at sort entry: #1491's family, noted there); `sort $by -$n`... is a term by the
sign rule now.  Guard rows Pl/t/sort-01.t 25-28, Pl/t/filetest-stack-01.t 18; the registry row Â§80.
